To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Δ9 desaturases of rose petals are involved in the degradation of membrane lipids of the senescing tissues.
the Δ9 desaturases are induced during senescence in the petals of rose.
a Δ9 fatty acid desaturase gene was identified and characterized in rose petals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology and biochemistry of senescence and abiotic stress tolerance in rose flowers.
the isolation and characterization of genes expressed in senescing petals of rose flowers, and with the elucidation of their functions.
the isolation of cDNAs for genes whose expression is specifically induced during the senescence of petals of Rosa hybrida.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the senescence of the rose petals is associated with the expression of a Δ9 desaturated enzyme, which is responsible for the conversion of palmitic to palmitoleic acid.
the Δ9 desaturases in plants are localized in the endoplasmic reticulum, and are involved in fatty acid desaturation in membrane lipids.
the expression of the Δ9 desaturases is a part of the senescence program of petals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the senescence of petals is associated with a massive degradation of lipids in the membranes, and that the degradation is accompanied by the induction of Δ9 desaturation of fatty acid moieties of membrane lipids.
the expression of Δ9 desaturation genes in rose petals was induced by ethylene.
the expression of a Δ9 desaturation gene is induced during senescence of rose petals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the senescence-associated gene is not expressed in petals until the petals begin to senesce.
senescence is an active process that requires energy, and that it involves the coordinated regulation of multiple metabolic pathways.
the expression of a homolog of the Δ9 desaturases in the petals of senescing roses may contribute to the degradation of membrane lipids during senescence.
